name: Wanderer
body:
From all walks of life and finding no path too dangerous to tread, wanderers travel the world without fear. Their grit and tenacity are as formidable as their methods. They might be a fierce marksman, a blade with no master, a gruff outlaw, or simply someone seeking to keep the peace. Their resolve and perseverance in the face of the bleakest odds make them an unrelenting foe and a reliable ally.

Alignment: Any.

Parent Classes: Gunslinger and swashbuckler.

Role: The wanderer is a warrior through-and-through but the expression of that combat prowess can be varied.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d10.

Starting Wealth: 5d6 × 10 gp (average 175 gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less. You also gain one weapon of your choice for which you have proficiency or gain proficiency at 1st level.

Class Skills

The wanderer’s class skills are Acrobatics (Dex), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (engineering) (Int), Knowledge (local) (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sleight of Hand (Dex), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Table 1: Wanderer Class Features

Class Features

The following are the class features of the wanderer.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Wanderers are proficient with simple and martial weapons, light armor, medium armor, and shields but not tower shields.

Grit (Ex)

You do what needs to be done, sometimes drawing unwanted attention. When others choose to bring you into their sights, you respond with the proper measure and focus called grit. In game terms, grit is a fluctuating measure of a gunslinger’s ability to perform amazing actions in combat. The wanderer’s grit functions differently than the grit from a gunslingerUC, instead of a pool that is full each day and refilled with extraordinary circumstances, the wanderer’s pool is empty outside of battle, but their maximum pool of grit is equal to their Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). During combat, the wanderer gains grit in the following ways:

The wanderer gains 1 point of grit when rolling initiative.
Anytime another creature, at the GM’s discretion, attacks or includes the wanderer in an offensive action, including Intimidate and Bluff checks.

The wanderer can learn other ways to gain grit through the preparedness ability, see below. When an encounter ends, all grit the wanderer had is lost. However, if combat resumes within 1 minute, the wanderer regains the grit they had at the end of the last encounter.

Grit is usable to activate the wanderer’s deeds, see below, though some deeds simply require grit to be in the wanderer’s pool.

Deeds (Ex)

At 1st level, a wanderer gains an extraordinary combat ability called a deed. Deeds are activated by expending grit during combat. However, each deed has a component that is active or usable without grit, including outside of combat. A wanderer gains an additional deed at 3rd level and every odd level thereafter.

The deeds are:

Fighter Training: A wanderer’s class levels count as fighter levels for the purposes of prerequisites.

Improved Initiative: At 1st level, a wanderer gains Improved Initiative as a bonus feat.

Weapon User: At 1st level, a wanderer may select one of the following feats as a bonus feat:

Weapon Focus with a simple or martial weapon.
Exotic Weapon Proficiency with a firearm and Gunsmithing
Exotic Weapon Proficiency with any other weapon
Rapid Reload
Quickdraw

At 2nd level, a wanderer gains Quickdraw as a bonus feat. If the wanderer already has Quickdraw, they may select another combat feat for which they meet the prerequisites.

Steely Demeanor (Ex)

At 2nd level, while in combat, a wanderer gains DR/- equal to 1/2 their current grit pool (minimum 1).

Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 3rd level, a wanderer gains the ability to react to danger before their senses would normally allow them to do so. They cannot be caught flat-footed, nor do they lose their Dex bonus to AC if the attacker is invisible. They still lose their Dexterity bonus to armor class if immobilized. A wanderer with this ability can still lose their Dexterity bonus to armor class if an opponent successfully uses the feint action against them.

If a wanderer already has uncanny dodge from a different class, they automatically gain improved uncanny dodge (see below) instead.

Bonus Feats

At 4th level, and every four levels thereafter, a wanderer gains a bonus feat in addition to those gained by normal advancement. These bonus feats must be combat or grit feats.

Preparedness (Ex)

At 4th level, a wanderer gains a new way to regain grit while in combat, selecting from the list of options below. A wanderer gains an additional method at 10th and 16th levels.

Ambush: You regain grit when you hit a target who has lost their Dex bonus to their AC.
Fantastic Hit: When you confirm a critical hit, you regain grit.
Moving Assault: You regain grit when you move more than 5 feet and attack in the same round.
Peacekeeper: You regain grit whenever you deal nonlethal damage to a target.
Reload: You regain grit whenever you reload a firearm you used within the last round of combat.
Takedown: You regain grit when you reduce an enemy, whose HD is at least 5 under yours, to 0 hit points or lower.
You’re Next: When you successfully use Intimidate to demoralize a target with an HD of 5 less than your HD or more.
Improved Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 6th level and higher, a wanderer can no longer be flanked. This defense denies a rogue the ability to sneak attack the wanderer by flanking them, unless the attacker has at least four more rogue levels than the target has wanderer levels.

If a character already has uncanny dodge (see above) from another class, the levels from the classes that grant uncanny dodge stack to determine the minimum rogue level required to flank the character.

Weapon Training (Ex)

At 6th level, a wanderer gains weapon training as the fighter ability of the same name. Every four levels thereafter, the wanderer gains increases to their weapon training ability and an additional weapon group exactly like the fighter does, but at a different level.

Stalwart (Ex)

At 8th level, a wanderer can use mental and physical resilience to avoid certain attacks. If they make a Fortitude or Will saving throw against an attack that has a reduced effect on a successful save, they instead avoid the effect entirely. This ability can only be used if the wanderer is wearing armor for which they are proficient. A helpless wanderer does not gain the benefit of the stalwart ability.

Improved Stalwart (Ex)

At 14th level, a wanderer’s stalwart ability improves, even on a failed fortitude or will saving throw against an attack the wanderer still only takes the reduced effect, if applicable.

True Grit (Ex)

At 20th level, a wanderer picks two deeds that they have and that they must spend grit to gain additional benefit. They can perform these deeds for 1 grit point fewer (minimum 0) than usual. If the number of grit points to perform a deed is reduced to 0, the wanderer can perform this deed as long as they have at least 1 grit point in their pool. If a deed could already be performed as long as they had at least 1 grit point in their pool, they can now perform that deed even when they have no grit points, including outside of combat.
